A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TinySQL with the same dataset framework and model families. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices support comparison despite substantial revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original fine-tuning accuracies, activation-patching experiments, EAP circuit ablations and SAE feature analyses, including appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds SAE circuit-recovery experiments, random-circuit comparisons, dataset analyses and LogitLens results.

M1.justification: v1 selects maximally activating SAE features and their highest-magnitude attention heads. v2 introduces adaptive similarity-guided feature ablation and decoder-norm/AUC mapping to select circuits containing attention heads and MLP neurons (Algorithm 1). This changes the circuit-identification procedure, while the base model families remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 adds CS4_Syn filtering with WHERE clauses and CS5_Syn multi-table JOIN queries, extending beyond v1's CS1–CS3 tasks. These additions are actually used for BM1 training and SAE evaluation, with results in Table 13. They address coverage explicitly missing in v1's limitations.

E2.justification: v2 adds random circuits as comparators for SAE–EAP overlap (Table 3) and EAP recovered accuracy, using circuits of comparable size (Table 18). This is a focused comparator addition; the existing base-model comparisons remain.

E3.justification: v2 adds evaluation protocols for SAE circuit recovery, cross-method overlap, retained-component percentages, random-circuit controls and layerwise token-score analysis. It also introduces linguistic dataset metrics. Shared fine-tuning splits and budgets, SAE training hyperparameters and the EAP batch-consistency protocol remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds circuit-identifiability and sparsity studies, SAE circuit ablations and LogitLens analyses across model-task configurations. Original activation-patching, MLP/full-layer ablations and SAE visualizations remain in the appendices. The newline-formatting shortcut case discussed in v1 is omitted.

E5.justification: Both versions use the same 15 batches of 100 prompts and consistency thresholds for EAP. v2's random-circuit averages are additional point estimates without disclosed repeat counts, dispersion, confidence intervals or significance tests; no changed uncertainty-reporting practice is established.

E6.justification: v2 newly reports SAE circuit recovery, including 82.19% on CS4 and 70.00% on CS5, along with random-circuit accuracies, overlap, sparsity, linguistic statistics and layerwise token-score trajectories. EAP Table 1 and full-model accuracies in v1 Table 4/v2 Table 7 are unchanged. v1 Table 2's field-token head-list results are omitted.

T1.justification: Algorithm 1 introduces decoder-norm weights and a cumulative-weight optimization rule for component selection. Section 5.2 also introduces an explicit local-minimality condition. No proof or guarantee establishing circuit minimality or identifiability is added.

C1.justification: v1 emphasizes circuit variability and interpretability-guided synthetic-data improvement. v2 makes five SQL subskills, circuit identifiability/local minimality and layered SQL composition central contributions. Dataset improvement disappears from the contribution list, although the overarching TinySQL testbed claim remains.

C2.justification: v2 interprets SAE–EAP overlap as evidence of alignment with ground-truth structure, develops a robustness–granularity interpretation of ablation and proposes staged SQL construction across layers. It removes the newline-artifact discussion and revises limitations toward incomplete circuit recovery, scaling difficulties and the absence of EAP analysis on CS4/5.

D1.justification: v2 adds model layer/head counts and clause-sampling and join-compatibility details in Appendices D–E. Shared fine-tuning implementation details remain. However, v1's controlled activation-patching setup and explicit BM2/BM3 SAE-release statement are omitted; this does not establish actual resource withdrawal.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for LogitLens, benchmark-language analysis, BIRD and linguistic metrics, while removing several activation-patching and ablation references. It adds linguistic positioning against existing benchmarks, but the main background and positioning between toy tasks and conventional text-to-SQL datasets remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract, contributions, SAE section, discussion and limitations are substantially rewritten. Dataset-generation sections move into Appendix C, activation-patching exposition is shortened, and the narrative is reorganized around circuit validation and layered generation. These changes substantially reshape the document beyond adding experiments.

P2.justification: v2 adds an algorithm box, LogitLens figures and tables covering circuit recovery, overlap, sparsity, random controls and dataset examples/statistics. Original plots and diagrams are retained, with v1's main-text ablation plots consolidated into Figure 17. The original field-head table is omitted, and the appendix displays are extensively rearranged.

improvement.justification: CS4/5 resolve v1's explicit lack of filters and joins, while new circuit ablations and random controls broaden validation. However, central new conclusions have unresolved support problems: Table 3 includes 70% SAE–EAP overlap versus 74.85% random overlap despite the claimed consistent advantage; Section 5.2 conflicts with Tables 2 and 4 on recovery and circuit size; and Figures 3 and 13 do not clearly support keyword-first generation. These substantive benefits coexist with weaker internal consistency and inadequately supported stronger claims, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
